title: Session KV aliasing experiment log
content:
Goal:
- Rapidly characterize a failure mode I saw on 2024-10-11 where long-context chat sessions produced 0-length tokens and then a hard kernel-selection mismatch causing request 503s. Suspect: slot aliasing (different sessions mapping to same physical KV slots) + attention kernel falling back to incompatible path.

Background / quick summary:
- Repro surfaced on dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-us-west-3-7) at medium load (~120 req/s).
- Model used: rwd-small-v2-qa (quantized path enabled via q8f).
- Symptoms: occasional token truncation, then "kernel-mismatch" traces in logs. Requests sometimes recover when restarted; other times session context gets corrupted and subsequent requests return nonsensical completions.

Environment notes:
- container: rwd/runtime:2024-10-02-0f9a3e (sha: 0f9a3e)
- kernel selector branch: feature/attention-routing-optim (commit: b4c2d9f)
- serving config: continuous-batching=true, kv-preserve-prefix=true, slot-count=16384, slot-shard=16
- hardware: A10G (driver 525.60), CUDA 12.1

Quick reproduction recipe (local stress):
1) Start local runtime with same env vars as ded pool: ./dev/run_local.sh --pool ded-sim --slot-count 16384 --preserve-prefix true
2) Run the repro client (scripts/repro/session-aliasing-client.py) with 4 concurrent sessions, each sending a 12k token prefix then an incremental prompt that appends ~200 tokens every request.
3) Observe logs for kernel-selector and kv-store messages: tail logs/runtime.log | grep -E "kernel-selector|kv-store|slot-alloc|alias"

Commands I ran (most relevant):
- reproduce: python3 scripts/repro/session-aliasing-client.py --concurrency 4 --rounds 40
- capture logs: kubectl logs -f pod/rwd-runtime-0 --since=1h | egrep "(kernel|kv|slot|alias)" > /tmp/alias-trace.txt
- lightweight trace: ./tools/bin/kvcapsule --dump-slots --session $SESSION_ID > /tmp/slot-dump.json

Observed snippets (copied raw):
- runtime.log snippet (2024-10-11T14:23:12Z):
  WARN kernel-selector: selected kernel "attn-v2-stream" but slot-format=compact-v1 (incompatible)
  ERROR kv-store: slot-alias-detected session=aq3t user=svc-x line=1492
  INFO request-12345 fallback: switching to cpu-emulation path

- kvcapsule dump (after session crash):
  "slots": [
    {"slot_id": 1042, "owner_session": "aq3t", "prefix_hash": "f3aa...", "valid_till": "2024-10-11T14:25:00Z"},
    {"slot_id": 1042, "owner_session": "b7fp", "prefix_hash": "d9c1...", "valid_till": "2024-10-11T14:24:58Z"}
  ]
  -> duplicated slot_id with different owner_session values (possible aliasing)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Allocation race where slot recycling code does not fully zero-out metadata before reassigning to new session; timing overlap allows two sessions to believe they own same slot (aliasing). Kernel selector reads slot-format and chooses an optimized attention kernel; if that kernel expects a different slot layout (e.g., compact-v2 vs compact-v1), we hit mismatch.
2) KV eviction + prefix-preserve path bug: when prefix-preserve=true, we try to keep prefix pointers but forget to update cache-format flag during cross-quantization migrations.
3) Off-by-one in slot-shard indexing when sequence length crosses internal threshold (e.g., 8192 tokens), causing wrap to a different shard and misread owner metadata.

Interim checks I did (and quick outcomes):
- Added assert in slot-assign code to reject non-zero metadata on assign (dev branch). Local repro slowed but didn't eliminate aliasing (++).
- Disabled preserve-prefix for a short run: aliasing frequency dropped by ~70% in a 6k request run. Suggests a strong correlation between preserve-prefix path and the bug.
- Force kernel-selector to only pick generic cpu path: eliminates the kernel-mismatch error but increases latency and does not fix slot duplication.

Next experiments to run (ordered):
A) Binary search on preserve-prefix code paths: add tracing at the moment we copy prefix pointers into the new slot object. Insert high-cardinality trace with slot-id and source-session. Run 10k request stress with preserve-prefix=true and false.
B) Reproduce with slot-count=32768 (double) to rule out wrap-around/alignment. If duplication rate drops proportionally, supports wrap hypothesis.
C) Add handshake between kernel-selector and kv-store: require a slot-format handshake (hash) before selecting an optimized kernel. This is a low-risk patch we can A/B via runtime flag.
D) Write a fuzz test targeting slot-assign under concurrent reclaim: tools/fuzz/slot_assign_fuzz.go (sketch exists).

Quick patch notes I sketched (for PR):
- enforce atomic slot metadata clear in reclaim path (use mutex per-slot or atomic CAS)
- emit slot-format id into session handshake token (small 4-byte tag)
- kernel-selector: validate slot-format tag vs expected kernel-profile; if mismatch => do not pick optimized kernel; log event with session & slot_id

Collateral traces / artifacts to attach when opening ticket: 
- /tmp/alias-trace.txt (logs)
- /tmp/slot-dump.json (kvcapsule output)
- recon client output: repro/outputs/2024-10-11-14-30.log
- small flamegraph for cpu fallback path (perf.data -> flame.svg)

Notes to self / questions:
- Is there any other place that writes owner_session metadata besides reclaim/assign? Need a grep across codebase: git grep "owner_session" -n || TODO
- Could HSM/KMS latency cause a timing window? Unlikely, but note why dedicated pool differs from local.
- If we add slot-format tag, ensure compatibility: older slots without tag must default to legacy-format.

Immediate action items (Today):
- Push trace-only patch to feature/kv-alias-trace and run 100k-request overnight in ded-sim. Assign: @Diego
- Draft PR for atomic reclaim (small, targeted). Assign: @Aisha (me)
- Create JIRA INF-5421 and attach artifacts above.

Timestamped breadcrumb (for future correlation):
- 2024-10-11T14:23 observed kernel-mismatch + slot alias
- 2024-10-12T09:12 initial local repro (small)
- 2024-10-20 patched trace-only branch and collected full dump

Free-form notes / hunches:
- The way we store prefix-hash in a side buffer (shared ring) could be racing: two threads reading/writing ring indices concurrently, producing inconsistent view. That would show up as prefix_hash differences for same slot_id (we observed that).
- If aliasing is rare at low concurrency but spikes as we hit interleaving between reclaim and assign, we can try synthetic microbench to isolate that window.

If anyone picks this up: start from reproduce recipe, attach logs to INF-5421, and ping me + Diego.

-- end of scratchpad (Aisha)
